activation-function.short: An activation function is a function that a neuron applies to its weighted sum, so that the network can bend straight lines.

adam.short: Adam is an optimizer that gives each weight its own step size, scaled by the typical size of its recent gradients.

attention.short: Attention lets each token take a weighted average of the other tokens, with weights that the model computes from the tokens.

backpropagation.short: Backpropagation finds the gradient of the loss for every weight in one pass backward through the network.

batch.short: A batch is a small group of samples that the model uses together in one training step.

bias.short: A bias is a parameter that a model adds to its result, so that the result can move up or down.

broadcasting.short: Broadcasting repeats a smaller grid of numbers, such as a bias, until it matches a larger grid, so that the two can be added.

chain-rule.short: The chain rule says that the rates of change along a chain of functions multiply.

channel.short: A channel is one grid of numbers of an image, for example its red values, its green values or its blue values.

class.short: A class is one of the possible answers of a classification task, for example one of the ten digits.

classification.short: Classification is the task of choosing one class for each input, for example the digit that an image shows.

confusion-matrix.short: A confusion matrix counts, for each true class, how often the model chose each class.

convolution.short: A convolution moves a small kernel over an image and computes a weighted sum at every position.

cross-entropy.short: Cross-entropy is a loss for classification, and it is minus the log of the probability that the model gives the right class.

data-set.short: A data set is a collection of samples, and each sample has an input and its target.

decision-boundary.short: The decision boundary is the line or curve where the answer of a model changes from one class to another.

embedding.short: An embedding is a vector that stands for a token, and training learns the numbers of this vector.

epoch.short: An epoch is one pass of training through every sample of the training set.

feature-map.short: A feature map is the grid of results of one kernel, and it shows where the pattern of the kernel appears in the image.

generalization.short: Generalization is how well a model works on new data that training did not use.

gradient.short: The gradient tells how much the loss changes when you change a weight by a small amount.

gradient-descent.short: Gradient descent improves a model in many small steps, and each step moves the weights downhill on the loss.

hidden-layer.short: A hidden layer is a layer between the input and the output of a network, so the data never shows its values.

hidden-points.short: Hidden points are examples that a model never trains on, so they show how well it works on new data.

kernel.short: A kernel is a small grid of weights that a convolution moves over an image to find one pattern.

layer.short: A layer is a group of neurons that all get the same inputs and compute their outputs side by side.

learning-rate.short: The learning rate is a small number that you choose, and it sets the size of each training step.

logit.short: A logit is the raw score that a model gives one class, before softmax changes the scores into probabilities.

loss.short: The loss is a number that measures how wrong the predictions of the model are.

matrix.short: A matrix is a grid of numbers in rows and columns, for example all the weights of a layer.

mean-squared-error.short: The mean squared error is a loss that squares the difference between each prediction and its target and then takes the mean.

mnist.short: MNIST is a well-known data set of small images of handwritten digits, and each image comes with the digit that it shows.

model.short: A model is a rule with adjustable numbers that turns an input into an answer, for example a score or a digit.

momentum.short: Momentum lets each step of gradient descent keep a part of the previous step, so the weights move in a steadier direction.

neural-network.short: A neural network is a model made of layers of neurons, and each layer gives its outputs to the next layer.

neuron.short: A neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs and adds a bias, and it often applies an activation function to the result.

optimizer.short: An optimizer is the part of a program that changes the parameters after each step, from their gradients.

overfitting.short: Overfitting means that a model fits the noise of its training set so closely that it gets worse on new data.

padding.short: Padding adds a border of zeros around an image, so that the kernel can also sit at the edges.

parameter.short: A parameter is an adjustable number in a model that training changes, for example a weight or a bias.

pixel.short: A pixel is one small square of an image, and its number tells how bright that square is.

prediction.short: A prediction is the output that a model gives for one input.

pretraining.short: Pretraining is the first stage of training a language model, where it learns to predict the next token of much text.

probability.short: A probability is a number from zero to one that tells how likely an event is.

relu.short: ReLU is an activation function that keeps a positive number and changes a negative number to zero.

sample.short: A sample is one item of a data set, for example one image of a digit together with the digit that it shows.

shape.short: The shape of a grid of numbers tells its size in each direction, for example two rows and three columns.

sigmoid.short: The sigmoid is an activation function that changes any number into a number between zero and one.

softmax.short: Softmax changes a list of scores into probabilities that are all positive and add to one.

stochastic-gradient-descent.short: Stochastic gradient descent is gradient descent where each step uses the gradient of one random batch in place of the whole data set.

stride.short: The stride is the number of pixels that a kernel moves between two positions.

target.short: The target is the right answer for one input, and the prediction of the model should come close to it.

tensor.short: A tensor is a grid of numbers with any number of directions, so vectors and matrices are special cases of it.

test-set.short: The test set is data that you keep apart until the end, and you use it once to measure the final model.

token.short: A token is a piece of text, often a word or a part of a word, that a language model reads as one unit.

training.short: Training changes the parameters of a model step by step, so that its loss gets smaller.

training-set.short: The training set is the part of the data that training uses to change the weights.

underfitting.short: Underfitting means that a model is too simple, or trained too little, to fit even its training set well.

validation-set.short: The validation set is data that training does not use, and you use it to make choices such as when to stop.

vector.short: A vector is a list of numbers in a given order, for example the inputs of a neuron.

weight.short: A weight is a parameter that a model multiplies with an input, so it sets how strongly that input counts.

weight-decay.short: Weight decay pulls each weight a little toward zero at every step, unless the data holds it up.
